clue.text: Perfect fathead, not at all well-behaved

parts.note: the head of the word fat, its first letter
someone lawless keeps to no rules at all

explanation.surface: A scornful remark about an idiot whose behaviour is anything but perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fathead' looks like an insult but splits into 'fat head': the head of FAT is F.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without a single flaw is perfect.

definitions.meaning: Stephen ... wrote Oh! Susanna and Camptown Races
to nurse an idea or a child is to nurture it, bring it up

explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Foster was a 19th-century American composer; to nurse a hope is to cherish and promote it.

indicators.note: repeatedly says the bill's letters come twice

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters go upward, read in reverse

parts.note: A1 (written AI) means first-rate, excellent

explanation.surface: A tree flourishing after repeated high bills.
explanation.definitionFit: The mimosa is a kind of wattle, a tree of this genus.

parts.note: reads like a pregnant animal, but points to a stretcher-like carrier and also a group of newborn animals

explanation.definitionFit: A litter is both a couch carried on poles and a set of young born together.

indicators.note: arrangement says the letters of the other entry are put into a new order

parts.note: the solution to 14 across supplies the letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to tidy up the layout of item fourteen.
explanation.definitionFit: To straighten something is to put it right, to adjust it.

clue.text: The learned fellow's German and in a hole

indicators.note: in tells us the German word sits inside the hole

parts.note: a pit is a hole in the ground
und is the German word for and

explanation.surface: A scholar of German extraction who has got himself into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A pundit is an expert or authority, a learned person.

parts.note: U stands for upper class, superior
praised means approved of, given approbation

explanation.surface: A high-ranking person promoted and showered with approval.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old label for upper-class usage, so it can stand for superior.
explanation.definitionFit: Upraised means raised up, lifted high.

clue.text: Deposit possibly a hundred — and that can be really hard!

indicators.note: possibly says the word may come in another order, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A geologist's remark about a sediment that may be rock-hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A despotic ruler is tyrannical, harsh and oppressive.

parts.note: tho is a short informal spelling of though, even if
rough means crude, without ceremony

explanation.surface: Someone who is careful though brusque.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thorough means paying attention to every detail.

parts.note: the letters of star, given a turn backwards, spell this exclamation

explanation.surface: Someone sees the best act on the bill and curses in disappointment.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, STAR TURN, and turning STAR round gives RATS.
explanation.definitionFit: The star turn is the main attraction and best act in a show.

clue.text: RAF officer accepting break with all speed

indicators.note: the officer takes in the break, so it goes inside his letters

parts.note: PO is short for Pilot Officer, a Royal Air Force rank
a rest is a break from work

explanation.surface: An air force officer agrees to a holiday very quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is the musical tempo marking meaning very fast.

clue.text: Pied mice could well become most common

indicators.note: the letters of the two words may turn into something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Speckled rodents might multiply until they are everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most common' defines an adjective: an epidemic disease or habit is widespread, the most prevalent one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something epidemic is rife and widespread, prevalent in a population.

clue.text: Casual garment for the weekend-the one and only one

parts.note: the end of the word week is its last letter
the Roman numeral for one is I
mono- is the prefix meaning single, only one

explanation.surface: Someone praising a favourite loungewear for relaxed Saturdays and Sundays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weekend' reads as Saturday and Sunday, but splits as 'week end', giving K.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose Japanese robe worn as a dressing gown is informal wear.

clue.text: A lack of generosity may appear smart in a letter

parts.note: to smart is to sting
ess is the spelt-out name of the letter S

explanation.surface: A mean-spirited, cutting remark might show up in correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' looks like an adjective meaning clever, but is the verb: to sting. 'in' is simply the letters IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinginess is meanness, an unwillingness to give.

indicators.note: arrangement says the letters of the other answer are put into a new order

parts.note: the solution to 4 down supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A cross-reference suggesting someone sorting things out is falling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Shattering, like cracking up, means breaking into pieces or collapsing.

clue.text: Summary of a sailing man's dissertation

parts.note: AB is short for able-bodied seaman
a tract is a treatise or dissertation

explanation.surface: A précis of a sailor's thesis.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstract is a brief summary of an academic paper.

clue.text: Oddly enough, set store by such favours

indicators.note: oddly says the words appear in a strange order, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Surprisingly, people value these prize ribbons highly.
explanation.walkthrough: A favour here is a ribbon or badge worn to show support, such as a rosette.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosettes are ribbon badges, favours worn at shows or by supporters.

clue.text: A mother going to market to get water

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
a sale is a market for goods

explanation.surface: A mother takes her produce to market to buy water.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is a jokey name for plain drinking water, the only drink of the first man.

parts.note: read as crops grown wide, a pun on a legume with a word meaning wide in its name

explanation.definitionFit: These are large flat legumes, a common garden vegetable.

indicators.note: absorbing says the comedian is taken inside the word for watch

parts.note: to see is to watch
a wag is a joker, a comedian

explanation.surface: Declining to watch a gripping stand-up act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb (decline) but is the noun: waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewage is waste matter carried off in drains.

clue.text: Virginia is quite incapable of being thoughtless

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
can't means cannot, quite unable to

explanation.surface: A woman named Virginia is too dim to think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virginia' looks like a woman's name but is the US state, VA.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacant look is empty of thought, blank.

parts.note: reads as encouragement after failure, but means a court trying a case again

explanation.definitionFit: To rehear a case is to give it a second judicial hearing.

indicators.note: the name of the play is acted out of its usual order, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actress has been cast as the Prince of Denmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is playing' suggests a role, but it rearranges the letters of HAMLET.
explanation.definitionFit: Thelma is a female first name.

parts.note: tide is an old word for a time or season, as in Eastertide
a race is a trial of speed

explanation.surface: A cycling time trial being held now.
explanation.definitionFit: A tide race is a fast-flowing stretch of tidal water, a strong current.

clue.text: A street light that's not in the right place

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A badly positioned street lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Astray means off course or misplaced.

indicators.note: back says the word for brought is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: led means brought or guided
aware means conscious

explanation.surface: Someone revived after fainting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LED into DEL. The definition is the last word: Delaware is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaware is one of the United States.

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An invigilator who frightens some of the exam candidates.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tests is an examiner.

clue.text: The agreeable individual a dolt put down

parts.note: an ass is a dolt, a fool
to enter is to put down in writing, to record

explanation.surface: A good-natured person got belittled by an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put down' suggests insulting, but means writing down: ENTER.
explanation.definitionFit: One who assents is someone who agrees.
